rationale: Acknowledged alert with no recorded investigation step is a textbook execution gap; matches the committed demo dataset (CSE-NEG).
Sub-60-second closure of critical alerts warrants inspection; matches CSE-EXEC in the committed demo dataset.
A case with zero investigation steps is either a data-quality problem or a genuine process gap; either way it needs a human look.
Closed alert with no disposition record leaves the closure decision unverifiable.
A critical/high asset producing zero alerts in the period is a plausible sensor-coverage failure, not evidence of safety.
Critical assets with sub-threshold alert volume should be checked for monitoring pipeline health.
Missing evidence categories block downstream analysis; request re-ingestion before drawing conclusions.
Investigation depth well below peer median is worth surfacing, though cohort size (n=3) limits confidence.
Robust-statistics outlier on investigation duration; surface for context, not an automatic verdict.
Template-cluster similarity is a supervisory signal requiring context, not inherent wrongdoing; this reviewer does not treat it as a standalone finding worth surfacing on its own in the demo dataset.
